newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate edges up on light speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate edges up on light speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 10 basis points to 19.45 percent in the late morning Friday after what traders said was light speculation following sharp falls during the prior session.
"Rates were very low, rock-bottom. There was a little speculation earlier, but the market could well stay where it is," a desk trader said.
Dealers said falling U.S. long bond yields had kept speculation at bay. The 30-year Treasury bond was up 25/32 this morning to yield 6.71 percent, in response to mild producer price data.
"You cannot rule out the levels at which the long bond is trading. That is helping money market rates to stay down," a fixed-income analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 30 basis points to 19.75 percent.

Liquidity of 942 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations. Nonetheless, dealers anticipated an outflow of 1.2 billion pesos due to demand for cash prior to the weekend.
